title: Softmax temperature
brief: Five queries ('the', 'a', 'on', 'by', 'it') and six candidate tokens ('cat', 'dog', 'sat', 'mat', 'ran', 'sun'), each a vector of width 8 drawn from N(0, 0.9²) with a fixed seed (rng(7): queries first, then keys). The score of token j for query i is the dot product q_i·k_j. Each row of scores becomes a probability distribution p = softmax(scores / τ). Left half: a 5×6 heatmap of p (sequential ramp, domain 0..1, values printed in the cells), rows labelled by query, columns by token. A highlight outlines one row and sweeps down the rows, 1.6 s per row, looping (the 'sweep' toggle pauses the sweep). Right half: a chip naming the highlighted query, τ in the corner, and a bar chart of that row's probabilities on a fixed 0..1 axis with the most likely token highlighted; optionally the raw scores under the bars ('showScores'). Controls: temperature τ (0.1–5), show scores, sweep. Presets: sharp (τ = 0.3), neutral (τ = 1), flat (τ = 3). Readouts: entropy of the highlighted row in bits (0 for a one-hot row, log₂ 6 ≈ 2.585 for uniform), its largest probability, its sum (always 1.000) and the most likely token.

beats.caption: Each row of scores becomes a distribution over the six tokens, and every row sums to 1.
Dividing by a small $\tau$ stretches the score gaps, so each row puts nearly all its weight on one token.
A large $\tau$ shrinks the gaps; the rows flatten towards $1/6$ and the entropy approaches $\log_2 6$.
